title: Set 56

sentences.ko: 신발까지 다 신고 나갈 준비를 끝냈는데 그때 동생한테 전화가 왔고, 통화 끊고 나니까 거의 여덟 시더라고. 이십 분 있자고 거기까지 차 몰고 가는 건 의미가 없어서 그냥 아침에 가려고. 이번엔 진짜로 갈 거야.
sentences.text: I had my shoes on and everything, and then my brother called, and by the time we got off the phone it was almost eight. There's no point driving all the way over there for twenty minutes, so I'm just going in the morning. I actually mean it this time.

alts.text: Shoes were on, I was ready to go, and then my brother called, and by the time we hung up it was almost eight. Not gonna drive all that way for twenty minutes, so I'm just going in the morning. I mean it this time, for real.

I had already put my shoes on, and then my brother called, and by the time we finished the call it was nearly eight. There is little sense in driving all that way for twenty minutes, so I will simply go in the morning. I do intend to go this time.

sentences.note: **and everything** 은 앞에서 말한 준비를 하나도 빠짐없이 다 해 놨다는 것을 강조하는 말입니다. **There's no point driving** 은 그렇게 차를 몰고 가 봐야 소용이 없다는 뜻입니다.
sentences.situation: 운동 가려다 말게 된 핑계 대기

sentences.ko: 빵 만들어 보겠다고 저울이며 좋은 밀가루며 다 사들였고, 처음 두 덩이는 아주 잘 나왔어. 그러더니 그냥 안 하게 되더라? 발효종은 봄부터 냉장고 안쪽에 그대로 처박혀 있는데 솔직히 열어 보기가 무서워.
sentences.text: I bought everything to start making bread, the scale, the good flour, all of it, and the first two loaves came out great. And then I just stopped? The starter's been sitting in the back of the fridge since spring and honestly I'm scared to open it.

alts.text: So I got all the bread stuff, the scale, the fancy flour, everything, and the first two loaves came out amazing. And then I just quit? That starter's been shoved in the back of the fridge since spring and honestly I'm kinda scared to open it.

I purchased everything required to begin baking bread, the scale, the good flour, all of it, and the first two loaves turned out very well. And then I simply stopped. The starter has been sitting at the back of the refrigerator since spring, and I confess I am afraid to open it.

sentences.note: **came out great** 는 만든 결과물이 아주 잘 나왔다는 말입니다. **been sitting in the back of the fridge** 는 냉장고 안쪽에서 손도 안 댄 채 방치돼 있다는 느낌을 줍니다.

sentences.ko: 오늘 밤에 길이 얼 거라고 하더라고. 그래서 대신 아침에 올라가려고. 깜깜한데 그 길을 가는 건 못 하겠어. 그러면 토요일 반나절은 날리는 셈이지만, 어디 도랑에 처박히는 것보다는 그게 나아.
sentences.text: They're saying it's going to ice over tonight, so we're driving up in the morning instead, because I'm not doing that road in the dark. That means we lose half of Saturday, but I'd take that over ending up in a ditch somewhere.

alts.text: Supposed to ice over tonight, so we're heading up in the morning instead, because no way am I doing that road in the dark. Yeah, we lose half of Saturday, but that beats ending up in a ditch somewhere.

They are forecasting ice tonight, so we will drive up in the morning instead, as I would rather not take that road in the dark. It does mean we lose half of Saturday, but I would prefer that to ending up in a ditch somewhere.

sentences.note: **ice over** 는 표면이 얼어붙는다는 뜻으로 길이나 창문에 씁니다. **I'd take that over** 는 둘을 놓고 차라리 이쪽을 택하겠다, 이게 더 낫다는 말입니다.

sentences.ko: 역 옆에 있는 데를 먼저 갔는데 줄이 가게 밖까지 나와 있어서 다른 데로 걸어갔더니, 테이블마다 죄다 누가 코트를 올려놨더라고. 결국 한 시간을 밖에서 추위에 떨며 앉아 있었어. 그러니까 나 내일 목소리 아프면 그래서 그런 줄 알아.
sentences.text: We tried the place by the station first and the line was out the door, so we walked over to the other one and every single table had somebody's coat on it. We ended up sitting outside for an hour in the cold, so if I sound sick tomorrow, you know why.

alts.text: First we hit the place by the station and the line was out the door, so we went over to the other one and every single table had somebody's coat on it. Wound up outside for an hour freezing, so if I sound sick tomorrow, that's why.

We tried the café near the station first, but the line extended out the door, so we walked to the other one, where every single table had somebody's coat on it. We ended up sitting outside for an hour in the cold, so if I sound unwell tomorrow, you will know the reason.

sentences.note: **the line was out the door** 는 줄이 가게 문밖까지 늘어설 만큼 길었다는 뜻입니다. **ended up sitting outside** 는 그럴 생각은 없었는데 결국 밖에 앉게 됐다는 말입니다.

sentences.ko: 나 이거 하나만 하고 일어날게. 내일 아침 여덟 시에 건조기 보러 사람이 오기로 했는데, 그 전에 저 벽장에서 짐을 다 꺼내 놔야 하거든. 너는 더 있어, 진짜로. 난 그냥 택시 타고 갈게.
sentences.text: I'm going to head out after this one. We've got somebody coming at eight in the morning about the dryer, and I still have to pull everything out of that closet before they get here. You stay, though, seriously, I'll just get a cab.

alts.text: Think I'm gonna take off after this one. Somebody's coming at eight in the morning about the dryer, and I've still got to pull everything out of that closet before they show up. You stay though, really, I'll just grab a cab.

I will be leaving after this one. Someone is coming at eight in the morning regarding the dryer, and I still need to remove everything from that closet before they arrive. Please do stay, I insist, I will simply take a taxi.

sentences.note: **head out** 은 자리에서 일어나 나선다는 뜻입니다. **grab a cab** 은 택시를 잡아탄다는 편한 말투로, take a taxi 보다 훨씬 일상적으로 씁니다.
sentences.situation: 저녁 모임에서 먼저 일어날 구실 만들기

reviewed: 1번 formal 의 "my brother telephoned" 는 요즘 원어민이 거의 쓰지 않는 옛 말투라 "called" 로 되돌렸습니다. 끝의 "keep to that" 도 어색해서 "I do intend to go this time" 으로 고쳤습니다.
2번 formal 의 "the better flour" 는 비교 대상이 없어 이상하게 읽혀서 text 와 같은 "the good flour" 로 맞췄습니다.
4번 formal 이 "the place" 를 "the restaurant" 로 바꿔 놓아 카페라는 상황과 어긋났습니다. "the café near the station" 으로 고쳤습니다.
